source_title: Breaking: Multiple feared dead, several hurt in horror crash near Byron Bay
source_excerpt:
Police are investigating the death of two people in a crash at Suffolk Park. ( Supplied )
Police are investigating whether one of the vehicles involved in a tragic fatal crash was driving erratically in the lead-up to the incident.
Emergency services were called to the scene on Broken Head Road, Suffolk Park just after 10:30am to reports of a three-vehicle crash.
Two people have died after a crash on Broken Head Road. ( Supplied )
On arrival, officers from the Tweed/Byron Police District found the driver of one vehicle, believed to be a woman in her 50s, had died.
The driver of a second vehicle, a man believed to be in his 60s, also died at the scene.
The passenger of the second vehicle, a woman in her 60s, was treated by NSW Ambulance paramedics and taken to Gold Coast University Hospital in a critical condition by the Westpac Helicopter.
The occupants of the third vehicle had minor injuries.
Police, firefighters and other emergency service crews are still at the scene of the crash. ( ABC News: Bruce Mackenzie )
Tweed/Byron Police District Inspector Matt Woods said it was a "horrendous scene".
"Initial investigations indicate two motor vehicles were travelling south on the correct side of the roadway and it appears a third motor vehicle, a maroon Nissan, has been travelling northbound on the incorrect side of the roadway and has collided head-on with one of the other cars, a white Kia," he said.
Inspector Woods said the two drivers died instantly.
He said police had interviewed a number of "independent witnesses" and were investigating reports of a person driving in an "erratic manner" on Broken Head Road before the crash.
"We have heard similar reports of that, and it is subject to the investigation," Inspector Woods said.
Police have established a crime scene and are investigating the crash.
District Inspector Matt Woods described the scene as horrendous. ( ABC News: Bruce Mackenzie )
Inspector Woods said it was a "combination" of local people and visitors involved in the crash.
He said the party in the white Kia was visiting from Western Australia and the female driving the maroon Nissan was from the Northern Rivers.
Two people from the Tweed Valley in a third vehicle involved in the crash were taken to Tweed Valley Hospital in a stable condition and treated for minor injuries.
Inspector Woods said there were a number of emergency service teams at the crash site, and many community members, who had witnessed the aftermath of the crash.
"It's a tragic incident that will have a flow-on to a number of families here," he said.
"I just extend my deepest condolences out to everyone involved and in particular the deceased people."
This month marks two decades since four teenagers were killed in a horrific crash on the same stretch of road.
Crosses mark the site of a 2006 crash on Broken Head Road. ( ABC North Coast: Samantha Turnbull )
On October 22, 2006, five boys celebrated a friend's birthday at a Chinese restaurant in Lismore before heading to Byron Bay.
Only the 17-year-old driver made it home.
Sixteen-year-olds Corey New and Paul Morris, and 17-year-olds Bryce Wells and Mitchell Eveleigh died after the car ran off the road just south of Byron Bay at Broken Head.
The driver was sentenced to four years in jail, with a non-parole period of two years.
As inquiries continue into today's crash, anyone with information or dashcam video is urged to contact Tweed/Byron police or Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000.
